sentences.zh: 劉瓛

translations.literal: Liu Huan
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huan

sentences.zh: 劉瓛字子珪，沛國相人，晉丹陽尹惔六世孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Huan, styled Zigui, was a man of Xiang in Pei Commandery and the sixth-generation descendant of Tan, Administrator of Danyang under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huan, styled Zigui, was a native of Xiang in Pei Commandery and a sixth-generation descendant of Tan, who had served as Administrator of Danyang under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖弘之，給事中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hongzhi was Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hongzhi had served as Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 父惠，治書御史。

translations.literal: His father Hui was Imperial Secretary for Drafting Documents.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui had served as Imperial Secretary for Drafting Documents.

sentences.zh: 瓛初州辟祭酒主簿。

translations.literal: Huan was first recruited by the province as Registrar to the Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was first recruited by the province to serve as Registrar to the Libationer.

sentences.zh: 宋大明四年，舉秀才，兄璲亦有名，先應州舉，至是別駕東海王元曾與瓛父惠書曰：「比歲賢子充秀，州閭可謂得人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming of Song, he was nominated as Outstanding Talent. His elder brother Sao was also renowned and had earlier responded to the provincial nomination. At this time the Vice Prefect Wang Yuanceng of Donghai wrote to Huan's father Hui: "In recent years your worthy sons have filled the quota of Outstanding Talent; the province and community may be said to have found the right men."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Daming era of Song (460), he was nominated as Outstanding Talent. His elder brother Sao was also well known and had already taken the provincial nomination in an earlier year. The Vice Prefect Wang Yuanceng of Donghai then wrote to Huan's father Hui: "In recent years your worthy sons have filled the quota of Outstanding Talent; the province and its people may truly be said to have found the right men."

sentences.zh: 」除奉朝請，不就。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Regular Attendant at Court but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed Regular Attendant at Court but declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 少篤學，博通《五經》。

translations.literal: From youth he devoted himself to study and mastered the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: From his youth he was devoted to learning and attained mastery of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 聚徒教授，常有數十人。

translations.literal: He gathered disciples to teach, and there were always several tens of them.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered students to instruct, and he usually had several dozen pupils at a time.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹袁粲於後堂夜集，瓛在座，粲指庭中柳樹謂瓛曰：「人謂此是劉尹時樹，每想高風；

translations.literal: Yuan Can, Administrator of Danyang, held a night gathering in the rear hall; Huan was among those present. Can pointed to a willow in the courtyard and said to Huan: "People say this is the tree from Administrator Liu's time; I always think of his lofty conduct;"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can, Administrator of Danyang, held an evening gathering in the rear hall, with Huan among the guests. Can pointed to a willow in the courtyard and said to Huan: "People say this is the tree from Administrator Liu's day; I often recall his lofty character;"

sentences.zh: 今復見卿清德，可謂不衰矣。

translations.literal: "now I again see your pure virtue—it may be said that it has not declined."
translations.idiomatic: "and now I see your pure virtue again—it may truly be said that it has not faded."

sentences.zh: 」薦爲祕書郎，不見用。

translations.literal: " He was recommended as Secretary in the Palace Library but was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: " He was recommended for the post of Secretary in the Palace Library but was not appointed.

sentences.zh: 除邵陵王郡主簿，安陸王國常侍，安成王撫軍行參軍，公事免。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Prince of Shaoling's commandery, Attendant of the Kingdom of Anlu, and Mobile Aide to the Pacification General of the Prince of Ancheng, and was dismissed for failure in official business.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chief Clerk in the Prince of Shaoling's commandery, Attendant of the Kingdom of Anlu, and Mobile Aide on the staff of the Prince of Ancheng's Pacification Army, but was dismissed for failing in his official duties.

sentences.zh: 瓛素無宦情，自此不復仕。

translations.literal: Huan had never had any desire for office, and from this time he never again entered service.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had never had any taste for official life, and from that point onward he never entered service again.

sentences.zh: 除車騎行參軍，南彭城郡丞，尚書祠部郎，竝不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Mobile Aide on the staff of the General of Chariots and Cavalry, Assistant in Nan Pengcheng Commandery, and Gentleman in the Ministry of Rites in the Department of Sacrifices, and in every case he declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Mobile Aide on the staff of the General of Chariots and Cavalry, Assistant in Nan Pengcheng Commandery, and Gentleman in the Sacrifices Section of the Ministry of Rites, but declined every appointment.

sentences.zh: 袁粲誅，瓛微服往哭，並致賻助。

translations.literal: When Yuan Can was executed, Huan went in plain dress to mourn him and also sent funeral gifts and aid.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Can was put to death, Huan went in plain dress to mourn him and also sent funeral gifts and assistance.

sentences.zh: 太祖踐阼，召瓛入華林園談語，謂瓛曰：「吾應天革命，物議以爲何如？

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor ascended the throne, he summoned Huan into the Hualin Garden for conversation and said to him: "I have received Heaven's mandate and carried out the revolution—what do people in general think of it?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao took the throne, he summoned Huan to the Hualin Garden for conversation and said to him: "I have received Heaven's mandate and carried out the revolution—what do people generally think of it?"

sentences.zh: 」瓛對曰：「陛下誡前軌之失，加之以寬厚，雖危可安；

translations.literal: " Huan replied: "Your Majesty takes warning from the errors of the previous track and adds to this a policy of leniency and generosity—even in danger one may be made secure;"
translations.idiomatic: " Huan replied: "Your Majesty takes warning from the mistakes of the previous regime and adds to this a policy of leniency and generosity—even in danger the realm may be made secure;"

sentences.zh: 若循其覆轍，雖安必危矣。

translations.literal: "if you follow their overturned track, even in security you will surely come to danger."
translations.idiomatic: "but if you follow their overturned path, even in security you will surely fall into danger."

sentences.zh: 」旣出，帝顧謂司徒褚淵曰：「方直乃爾！

translations.literal: " After he had left, the Emperor turned and said to the Minister of Education Chu Yuan: "So upright and square is he!"
translations.idiomatic: " After Huan had left, the emperor turned and said to Minister of Education Chu Yuan: "How upright and forthright he is!"

sentences.zh: 學士故自過人。

translations.literal: "A scholar is of course superior to other men."
translations.idiomatic: "A scholar is naturally a cut above ordinary men."

sentences.zh: 」敕瓛使數入，而瓛自非詔見，未嘗到宮門。

translations.literal: " He ordered Huan to come in frequently, but unless summoned by imperial edict Huan never came to the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Huan to visit the palace often, but unless summoned by imperial edict Huan never came to the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 上欲用瓛爲中書郎，使吏部尚書何戢喻旨。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to employ Huan as Secretariat Gentleman and had the Minister of the Ministry of Officials He Jian convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to appoint Huan Secretariat Gentleman and had Minister of Officials He Jian convey his intent.

sentences.zh: 戢謂瓛曰：「上意欲以鳳池相處，恨君資輕，可且就前除，少日當轉國子博士，便卽後授。

translations.literal: Jian said to Huan: "His Majesty wishes to place you in the Phoenix Pool; he regrets that your qualifications are light. You may for the moment accept the previous appointment; in a few days you will be transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University, and then the later post will be conferred at once."
translations.idiomatic: Jian said to Huan: "His Majesty wishes to place you in the Secretariat—the Phoenix Pool—but regrets that your seniority is still slight. You may accept the previous appointment for the moment; in a few days you will be transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University, and the higher post will follow immediately thereafter."

sentences.zh: 」瓛曰：「平生無榮進意，今聞得中書郎而拜，豈本心哉！

translations.literal: " Huan said: "All my life I have had no wish for glory or advancement; now to hear that I am to receive the post of Secretariat Gentleman and bow to accept it—how could that be my true heart!"
translations.idiomatic: " Huan said: "All my life I have had no wish for glory or advancement; to hear that I am to receive the post of Secretariat Gentleman and bow to accept it—how could that be my true intent!"

sentences.zh: 」後以母老闕養，重拜彭城郡丞。

translations.literal: " Later, because his mother was old and he lacked means to support her, he again accepted appointment as Assistant in Pengcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " Later, because his mother was elderly and he lacked means to support her, he again accepted appointment as Assistant in Pengcheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 謂司徒褚淵曰：「自省無廊廟之才，所願唯保彭城丞耳。

translations.literal: He said to the Minister of Education Chu Yuan: "On examining myself I have no talent for the court and hall; all I wish is merely to keep the post of Assistant in Pengcheng."
translations.idiomatic: He said to Minister of Education Chu Yuan: "When I examine myself, I have no talent for high office; all I wish is simply to keep the post of Assistant in Pengcheng."

sentences.zh: 」上又以瓛兼總明觀祭酒，除豫章王驃騎記室參軍，丞如故，瓛終不就。

translations.literal: " The Emperor also made Huan concurrently Libationer of the Zongming Observatory and appointed him Recorder on the staff of the Prince of Yuzhang's Rapid Cavalry; his assistant post was to remain as before, but Huan in the end did not take up office.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor also made Huan concurrently Libationer of the Zongming Observatory and appointed him Recorder on the staff of the Prince of Yuzhang's Rapid Cavalry, with his assistant post unchanged—but Huan ultimately declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 武陵王曅爲會稽太守，上欲令瓛爲曅講，除會稽郡丞，學徒從之者轉衆。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ye, was Grand Administrator of Kuaiji; the Emperor wished to have Huan lecture for Ye and appointed him Assistant in Kuaiji Commandery, and the disciples who followed him grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ye, became Grand Administrator of Kuaiji, the emperor wished Huan to serve as his lecturer and appointed him Assistant in Kuaiji Commandery; the students who followed him grew ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 永明初，竟陵王子良請爲征北司徒記室。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongming era, the Prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, requested him as Recorder on the staff of the Minister of Education, Pacification General of the North.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongming era, the Prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, requested him as Recorder on the staff of the Pacification General of the North and Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 瓛與張融王思遠書曰：「奉教使恭召，會當停公事，但念生平素抱，有乖恩顧。

translations.literal: Huan wrote to Zhang Rong and Wang Siyuan: "I have received instruction and a respectful summons; I ought to suspend official business, but I reflect on the lifelong disposition I have cherished, which runs counter to this gracious regard."
translations.idiomatic: Huan wrote to Zhang Rong and Wang Siyuan: "I have received your instruction and a respectful summons; I ought to set aside official business, but when I reflect on the disposition I have cherished all my life, it runs counter to this gracious attention."

sentences.zh: 吾性拙人閒，不習仕進，昔嘗爲行佐，便以不能及公事免黜，此皆眷者所共知也。

translations.literal: "My nature is awkward among men and I am unused to advancing in office; formerly I once served as a mobile aide and was dismissed and removed for inability to attend to official business—this is what those who care for me all know together."
translations.idiomatic: "My nature is awkward among men, and I am unused to pursuing office; I once served as a mobile aide and was dismissed for failing to keep up with official business—this is something all who know me are aware of."

sentences.zh: 量己審分，不敢期榮。

translations.literal: "Having measured myself and examined my allotment, I dare not hope for glory."
translations.idiomatic: "Having measured my abilities and examined my proper place, I dare not hope for glory."

sentences.zh: 夙嬰貧困，加以疏懶，衣裳容髮，有足駭者。

translations.literal: "From long ago I have been afflicted with poverty and want, and to this I add negligence and indolence; my clothes, appearance, and hair are enough to startle one."
translations.idiomatic: "I have long suffered poverty and want, and on top of that I am negligent and indolent; my clothing, appearance, and hair are enough to shock anyone who sees them."

sentences.zh: 中以親老供養，褰裳徒步，脫爾逮今，二代一紀。

translations.literal: "In the midst of this, because my parents were old and needed support, I lifted my robes and went on foot; thus it has continued until today—two reigns and one full cycle of years."
translations.idiomatic: "In the meantime, because my parents were elderly and needed support, I went on foot with my robes hitched up; in this way it has continued until today—two reigns and a full generation."

sentences.zh: 先朝使其更自脩正，勉厲於階級之次，見其襤縷，或復賜以衣裳，袁、褚諸公咸加勸勵，終不能自反也。

translations.literal: "The previous court had him further correct himself and exert himself in the ranks of office; seeing his ragged clothes, they would again bestow garments upon him. Gentlemen such as Yuan and Chu all added encouragement, yet in the end he could not turn himself around."
translations.idiomatic: "The previous court urged him to reform himself and strive within the ranks of office; seeing his ragged clothes, they would sometimes bestow garments upon him. Gentlemen such as Yuan and Chu all encouraged him, yet in the end he could not change his ways."

sentences.zh: 一不復爲，安可重爲哉？

translations.literal: "Once one does not do a thing again, how can one do it a second time?"
translations.idiomatic: "Once one has refused to do a thing, how can one do it again?"

sentences.zh: 昔人有以冠一免不重加於首，每謂此得進止之儀。

translations.literal: "In antiquity there was one who, having once removed his cap, would not put it on his head again; I always say that in this one grasps the ritual of advancing and stopping."
translations.idiomatic: "In antiquity there was a man who, having once removed his cap, would not place it on his head again; I have always held that in this one grasps the proper ritual of advancing and withdrawing."

sentences.zh: 古者以賢制爵，或有秩滿而辭老，以庸制祿，或有身病而求歸者，永瞻前良，在己何若。

translations.literal: "In antiquity worthies were used to regulate ranks of nobility; some, when their term was full, resigned on account of age. Merit was used to regulate emoluments; some, when their bodies were ill, sought to return home. I forever look up to the worthies of old—how do I compare to them?"
translations.idiomatic: "In antiquity worthies were used to regulate noble ranks; some, when their term was complete, resigned on account of age. Merit was used to regulate stipends; some, when ill in body, sought to return home. I forever look up to the worthies of old—how do I measure against them?"

sentences.zh: 又上下年尊，益不願居官次，廢晨昏也。

translations.literal: "Moreover, my elders above and below me in years are venerable; all the more do I not wish to occupy a place in the official hierarchy and neglect the morning and evening duties."
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover, my elders are advanced in years; all the more do I not wish to hold a place in the official hierarchy and neglect my morning and evening duties to them."

sentences.zh: 先朝爲此，曲申從許，故得連年不拜榮授，而帶帖薄祿。

translations.literal: "The previous court, on this account, bent its will and granted permission, so that for successive years I did not accept honored appointments but carried a nominal post with a slender stipend."
translations.idiomatic: "On this account the previous court bent its will and granted permission, so that for years I did not accept honored appointments but held a nominal post with a slender stipend."

sentences.zh: 旣習此歲久，又齒長疾侵，豈宜攝齋河閒之聽，廁迹東平之僚？

translations.literal: "Having grown accustomed to this for many years, and with my years advanced and illness encroaching, how could it be fitting to fast and take my place in the Prince of Hejian's audience hall or stand among the Prince of Dongping's subordinates?"
translations.idiomatic: "Having grown accustomed to this for many years, and with my years advanced and illness encroaching, how could it be fitting to observe fasts and take my place in the Prince of Hejian's audience hall, or stand among the Prince of Dongping's staff?"

sentences.zh: 本無絕俗之操，亦非能偃蹇爲高，此又諸賢所當深察者也。

translations.literal: "I fundamentally have no conduct of transcending the vulgar, nor am I able to be proud and aloof to make myself lofty—this too is what you gentlemen ought to examine deeply."
translations.idiomatic: "I have no conduct of transcending the world, nor am I able to be proud and aloof to set myself above others—this too is what you gentlemen ought to examine carefully."

sentences.zh: 近奉初教，便自希得託迹於客遊之末，而固辭榮級，其故何耶？

translations.literal: "Recently, having received the first instruction, I myself hoped to entrust my traces to the end of guest wanderers, yet I firmly decline honored rank—what is the reason?"
translations.idiomatic: "Recently, having received your first instruction, I hoped to place myself among traveling guests at court, yet I firmly decline honored rank—what is the reason?"

sentences.zh: 以古之王侯大人，或以此延四方之士，甚美者則有輻湊燕路，慕君王之義，驤鑣魏闕，高公子之仁，繼有追申、白而入楚，羨鄒枚而遊梁，吾非敢叨夫曩賢，庶欲從九九之遺蹤。

translations.literal: "Because ancient kings, marquises, and great men sometimes used this means to draw scholars from the four quarters: the most admirable would gather like spokes on the road to Yan, admiring a lord-king's righteousness and prancing their steeds to the Wei Gate; they would exalt a lord-son's benevolence, and in succession there were those who followed Shen and Bai into Chu and envied Zou and Mei in wandering to Liang. I do not dare claim those former worthies; I merely wish to follow the lingering traces of the nine-nines."
translations.idiomatic: "Ancient kings, marquises, and great men sometimes used this means to draw scholars from all directions: the finest would gather like spokes on the road to Yan, drawn by a lord's righteousness and prancing their steeds to the Wei Gate; they would honor a prince's benevolence, and in succession men followed Shen and Bai into Chu and envied Zou and Mei in traveling to Liang. I do not dare claim those former worthies; I merely wish to follow their lingering example."

sentences.zh: 旣於聞道集泮不殊，而幸無職司拘礙，可得奉溫凊，展私計，志在此爾。

translations.literal: "Since in hearing the Way and gathering at the school there is no difference, yet fortunately there is no office or duty to constrain me, I may attend to warmth and coolness and carry out private plans—my aim is in this alone."
translations.idiomatic: "Since in hearing the Way and gathering at the school there is no difference, yet fortunately I am not constrained by official duties, I may attend to my parents' comfort and carry out my private plans—my aim lies in this alone."

sentences.zh: 」除步兵校尉，並不拜。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers and again did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers and again declined to accept.

sentences.zh: 瓛姿狀纖小，儒學冠於當時，京師士子貴遊莫不下席受業。

translations.literal: Huan's stature was slight and small, but his Confucian learning topped his age; the scholars and noble wanderers of the capital all sat below his mat to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was slight in stature, but his Confucian learning stood at the head of his age; scholars and noble visitors in the capital all sat below his mat to receive instruction.

sentences.zh: 性謙率通美，不以高名自居。

translations.literal: By nature he was modest, straightforward, and thoroughly admirable, and did not take his lofty reputation upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was modest, straightforward, and thoroughly admirable, and did not rest on his lofty reputation.

sentences.zh: 遊詣故人，唯一門生持胡牀隨後，主人未通，便坐問答。

translations.literal: When he went to visit old acquaintances, only one disciple followed behind carrying a folding stool; before the host had announced him, he would sit down and engage in question and answer.
translations.idiomatic: When he visited old acquaintances, only one disciple followed behind carrying a folding stool; before the host had even announced him, he would sit down and converse.

sentences.zh: 住在檀橋，瓦屋數閒，上皆穿漏。

translations.literal: He lived at Tan Bridge in several tiled rooms, all of whose roofs were pierced and leaking.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at Tan Bridge in a few tiled rooms whose roofs were all pierced and leaking.

sentences.zh: 學徒敬慕，不敢指斥，呼爲青溪焉。

translations.literal: His disciples revered and admired him and did not dare point it out directly, calling it instead the Green Stream.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples revered him and did not dare point it out directly, calling his dwelling instead the Green Stream.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良親往脩謁。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, went in person to pay a respectful visit.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, went in person to pay him a respectful visit.

sentences.zh: 七年，表世祖爲瓛立館，以揚烈橋故主第給之，生徒皆賀。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he memorialized Emperor Wu to establish a hall for Huan and had the former lord's mansion at Yanglie Bridge given to him; the disciples all congratulated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he memorialized Emperor Wu to establish a hall for Huan and had the former lord's mansion at Yanglie Bridge assigned to him; all his disciples congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 瓛曰：「室美爲人災，此華宇豈吾宅邪？

translations.literal: Huan said: "A beautiful dwelling becomes a man's disaster—how could this splendid house be my residence?"
translations.idiomatic: Huan said: "A beautiful dwelling becomes a man's disaster—how could this splendid house be my home?"

sentences.zh: 幸可詔作講堂，猶恐見害也。

translations.literal: "It would be fortunate if an edict could make it a lecture hall; I still fear I would come to harm."
translations.idiomatic: "It would be fortunate if an edict could make it a lecture hall; I still fear I would come to harm by it."

sentences.zh: 」未及徙居，遇病，子良遣從瓛學者彭城劉繪、從陽范縝將曅於瓛宅營齋。

translations.literal: " Before he could move his residence he fell ill. Ziliang sent Liu Hui of Pengcheng and Fan Zhen of Congyang, who had studied under Huan, to lead the fast at Huan's house.
translations.idiomatic: " Before he could move in he fell ill. Ziliang sent Liu Hui of Pengcheng and Fan Zhen of Congyang, who had studied under Huan, to conduct the fast at Huan's house.

sentences.zh: 及卒，門人受學者並弔服臨送。

translations.literal: When he died, his disciples and those who had received instruction from him all wore mourning dress and came to escort him to the grave.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his disciples and students all wore mourning dress and came to escort him to the grave.

sentences.zh: 時年五十六。

translations.literal: He was fifty-six years old at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-six at the time.

sentences.zh: 瓛有至性，祖母病疽經年，手持膏藥，漬指爲爛。

translations.literal: Huan had utmost filial nature: his grandmother suffered from a carbuncle for a full year, and he held the medicinal paste in his hand until his fingers were soaked and rotted.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was deeply filial: his grandmother suffered from a carbuncle for a full year, and he held the medicinal paste in his hand until his fingers were soaked through and rotted.

sentences.zh: 母孔氏甚嚴明，謂親戚曰：「阿稱便是今世曾子。

translations.literal: His mother, née Kong, was very strict and clear-minded; she said to relatives: "A Cheng is truly the Zengzi of the present age."
translations.idiomatic: His mother, of the Kong clan, was very strict and principled; she told relatives: "A Cheng is truly the Zengzi of our age."

sentences.zh: 」阿稱，瓛小名也。

translations.literal: " A Cheng was Huan's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: " A Cheng was Huan's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，未有婚對。

translations.literal: When he was past forty he still had no marriage arranged.
translations.idiomatic: Past the age of forty, he still had no marriage arranged.

sentences.zh: 建元中，太祖與司徒褚淵爲瓛娶王氏女。

translations.literal: During the Jianyuan era, the Grand Progenitor and the Minister of Education Chu Yuan arranged for Huan to marry a daughter of the Wang clan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyuan era, Emperor Gao and Minister of Education Chu Yuan arranged for Huan to marry a daughter of the Wang clan.

sentences.zh: 王氏椓壁掛履，土落孔氏牀上，孔氏不悅，瓛卽出其妻。

translations.literal: The Wang woman hammered the wall to hang her shoes, and earth fell onto Lady Kong's bed. Lady Kong was displeased, and Huan at once sent his wife away.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang woman hammered the wall to hang her shoes, and dirt fell onto Lady Kong's bed. Lady Kong was displeased, and Huan immediately sent his wife away.

sentences.zh: 及居父喪，不出廬，足爲之屈，杖不能起。

translations.literal: When he was in mourning for his father, he did not leave the mourning hut; his feet became bent from it, and he could not rise even with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: When he was in mourning for his father, he did not leave the mourning hut; his feet became bent from the strain, and he could not rise even with a staff.

sentences.zh: 今上天監元年，下詔爲瓛立碑，諡曰貞簡先生。

translations.literal: In the present reign, in the first year of Tianjian, an edict was issued to erect a stele for Huan, and he was given the posthumous title Master of Upright Simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: In the present reign, in the first year of Tianjian (502), an edict was issued to erect a stele for Huan, posthumously titled Master of Upright Simplicity.

sentences.zh: 所著文集，皆是禮義，行於世。

translations.literal: The collected writings he authored were all on ritual and righteousness and circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings were all on ritual and righteousness and circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 初，瓛講《月令》畢，謂學生嚴植曰：「江左以來，陰陽律數之學廢矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huan had finished lecturing on the Monthly Ordinances, he said to his student Yan Zhi: "Since the east of the Yangtze, the study of yin and yang and pitch-pipes and numbers has fallen into disuse."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Huan had finished lecturing on the Monthly Ordinances, he told his student Yan Zhi: "Since the establishment of the Eastern Jin, the study of yin and yang, pitch-pipes, and calendrical numbers has fallen into disuse."

sentences.zh: 吾今講此，曾不得其髣彿。

translations.literal: "Now that I lecture on this, I have never even grasped its dim outline."
translations.idiomatic: "Now that I lecture on this, I have never even grasped its dim outline."

sentences.zh: 」時濟陽蔡仲熊禮學博聞，謂人曰：「凡鍾律在南，不容復得調平。

translations.literal: " At that time Cai Zhongxiong of Jiyang, broad in learning on ritual, said to people: "Whenever pitch-pipes and bells are in the south, they cannot again be brought to proper tuning and balance."
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Cai Zhongxiong of Jiyang, renowned for his learning in ritual, told people: "Whenever pitch-pipes and bells are in the south, they cannot again be brought to proper tuning."

sentences.zh: 昔五音金石，本在中土；

translations.literal: "In former times the five tones and metal and stone instruments were originally in the central land;"
translations.idiomatic: "In former times the five tones and metal and stone instruments belonged to the central lands;"

sentences.zh: 今旣來南，土氣偏陂，音律乖爽。

translations.literal: "now that we have come south, the qi of the soil is skewed and sloping, and pitch and regulation are out of accord."
translations.idiomatic: "now that we have come south, the soil's qi is skewed, and pitch and regulation are out of accord."

sentences.zh: 」瓛亦以爲然。

translations.literal: " Huan also considered this correct.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan also agreed.

sentences.zh: 仲熊歷安西記室，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Zhongxiong successively served as Recorder on the staff of the Pacification General of the West and as Left Assistant in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiong served successively as Recorder on the staff of the Pacification General of the West and as Left Assistant in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 瓛弟璡。

translations.literal: Huan's younger brother Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's younger brother Jin.

translations.literal: [=] Section divider in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: [=] Section divider in the source text.

sentences.zh: 弟璡

translations.literal: Younger brother Jin
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Jin

sentences.zh: =璡字子璥。

translations.literal: [=] Jin, styled Zijun.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, styled Zijun.

sentences.zh: 方軌正直。

translations.literal: He matched the square track and was upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was square in conduct and upright in character.

sentences.zh: 宋泰豫中，爲明帝挽郎。

translations.literal: During the Taiyu era of Song, he served as a dirge-bearer for Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiyu era of Song, he served as a dirge-bearer at Emperor Ming's funeral.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，建平王景素征北主簿，深見禮遇。

translations.literal: He was nominated as Outstanding Talent and became Chief Clerk to the Pacification General of the North for the Prince of Jianping, Jing Su, and was deeply honored and treated well.
translations.idiomatic: He was nominated as Outstanding Talent and served as Chief Clerk to the Pacification General of the North on the staff of the Prince of Jianping, Jing Su, and was deeply honored.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王征虜安南行參軍。

translations.literal: He was Mobile Aide on the Pacification General and Pacifier of the South staff of the Prince of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Mobile Aide on the Pacification General and Pacifier of the South staff of the Prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 建元初，爲武陵王曅冠軍征虜參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan, he was Aide on the Champion and Pacification General staff of the Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ye.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyuan era, he served as Aide on the Champion and Pacification General staff of the Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ye.

sentences.zh: 曅與僚佐飲，自割鵝炙。

translations.literal: Ye was drinking with his staff officers and personally carved roast goose.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was drinking with his staff and personally carved roast goose.

sentences.zh: 璡曰：「應刃落俎，膳夫之事，殿下親執鸞刀，下官未敢安席。

translations.literal: Jin said: "That the blade should fall and meat drop to the board is the cook's business; Your Highness personally holds the imperial carving knife—your humble officer does not dare sit at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Jin said: "For meat to fall from the blade to the board is the cook's task; Your Highness personally holds the carving knife—I dare not remain seated at ease."

sentences.zh: 」因起請退。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he rose and asked to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he rose and asked to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 與友人孔澈同舟入東，澈留目觀岸上女子，璡舉席自隔，不復同坐。

translations.literal: With his friend Kong Che he shared a boat going east; Che kept his eyes on a woman on the shore. Jin raised his mat to separate himself and would not sit together again.
translations.idiomatic: With his friend Kong Che he shared a boat traveling east; Che kept his eyes on a woman on the shore. Jin raised his mat to separate himself and would not sit with him again.

sentences.zh: 豫章王太尉板行佐。

translations.literal: He was Mobile Aide on the Grand Marshal's staff board of the Prince of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Mobile Aide on the Grand Marshal's staff of the Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 兄瓛夜隔壁呼璡共語，璡不答，方下牀著衣立，然後應。

translations.literal: His elder brother Huan at night called through the wall for Jin to converse; Jin did not answer, but first got down from his bed, put on his clothes, and stood—only then did he respond.
translations.idiomatic: At night his elder brother Huan called through the wall for Jin to talk; Jin did not answer at once but first got down from his bed, dressed, and stood—only then did he respond.

sentences.zh: 瓛問其久，璡曰：「向束帶未竟。

translations.literal: Huan asked why he had been so long; Jin said: "Just now I had not yet finished girding my sash."
translations.idiomatic: Huan asked why he had taken so long; Jin said: "I had not yet finished tying my sash."

sentences.zh: 」其立操如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the conduct he established.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the standard of conduct he maintained.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子召璡入侍東宮，每上事，輙削草。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenxiao summoned Jin to attend in the Eastern Palace; whenever he submitted a memorial, he would always revise the draft.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenxiao summoned Jin to serve in the Eastern Palace; whenever he submitted a memorial, he would always revise the draft himself.

sentences.zh: 尋署中兵，兼記室參軍大司馬軍事，射聲校尉，卒官。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Central Troops Commander, concurrently Recorder, staff officer on the Grand Marshal's military staff, and Commandant of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Central Troops Commander, concurrently Recorder and staff officer on the Grand Marshal's military staff, and Commandant of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 陸澄

translations.literal: Lu Cheng
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cheng

sentences.zh: 陸澄字彥淵，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Lu Cheng, styled Yanyuan, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cheng, styled Yanyuan, was a native of Wu in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖邵，臨海太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao was Grand Administrator of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shao had served as Grand Administrator of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 父瑗，州從事。

translations.literal: His father Yuan was a provincial aide.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan had served as a provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 澄少好學，博覽無所不知，行坐眠食，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: From youth Cheng loved learning; he read broadly and there was nothing he did not know. Walking, sitting, sleeping, or eating, his hand never released his scroll.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Cheng loved learning; he read widely and there was scarcely anything he did not know. Whether walking, sitting, sleeping, or eating, he never let go of his scroll.

sentences.zh: 起家太學博士，中軍衞軍府行佐，太宰參軍，補太常丞，郡主簿，北中郎行參軍。

translations.literal: He began his career as Erudite of the Imperial University, Mobile Aide in the General of the Center and General of the Guards offices, Aide on the Grand Mentor's staff, supplemented as Assistant in the Ministry of Ceremonies, Chief Clerk of a commandery, and Mobile Aide on the North General of the Household staff.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Erudite of the Imperial University, then served as Mobile Aide in the offices of the General of the Center and General of the Guards, as Aide on the Grand Mentor's staff, as Assistant in the Ministry of Ceremonies, as Chief Clerk of a commandery, and as Mobile Aide on the North General of the Household staff.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始初，爲尚書殿中郎，議皇后諱及下外，皆依舊稱姓。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi of Song, he became Palace Attendant in the Masters of Writing; in discussing the taboo name of the empress and those outside the palace, all followed the old practice of using surnames.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taishi era of Song, he served as Palace Attendant in the Masters of Writing; in deliberations on the empress's taboo name and those outside the palace, all followed the old practice of using surnames.

sentences.zh: 左丞徐爰案司馬孚議皇后不稱姓，春秋逆王后于齊，澄不引典據明，而以意立議，坐免官，白衣領職。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Xu Ai cited Sima Fu's discussion that the empress does not use her surname, and that in Spring and Autumn the queen was moved against to Qi. Cheng did not cite classic evidence clearly but established the discussion by personal opinion; on this account he was removed from office and served in plain clothes while retaining his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Xu Ai cited Sima Fu's argument that the empress does not use her surname, and that in the Spring and Autumn Annals the queen was moved against to Qi. Cheng failed to cite clear classical evidence and instead based his position on personal opinion; for this he was dismissed from office and served in plain clothes while retaining his duties.

sentences.zh: 郎官舊有坐杖，有名無實，澄在官積前後罰，一日幷受千杖。

translations.literal: For gentleman officials there was an old regulation of sitting punishment with the stick—in name but not in fact. While Cheng was in office he accumulated penalties from before and after; in one day he received a thousand stick-strokes altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman officials had an old regulation of sitting stick punishment that existed in name only. While Cheng held office he accumulated penalties from earlier and later cases and in one day received a thousand strokes of the stick altogether.

sentences.zh: 轉通直郎，兼中書郎，尋轉兼左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Direct Communication Gentleman, concurrently Secretariat Gentleman, and soon transferred to concurrently Left Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Direct Communication Gentleman and concurrently Secretariat Gentleman, and soon afterward was made concurrent Left Assistant.

sentences.zh: 泰始六年，詔皇太子朝賀服衮冕九章，澄與儀曹郎丘仲起議：「服冕以朝，實著經文。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi, an edict ordered that the crown prince wear the nine emblems of the robe and cap with tassels when attending court congratulations. Cheng and Qiu Zhongqi of the Rituals Section discussed: "Wearing the cap with tassels to attend court is in fact set forth in the canonical texts."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taishi, an edict ordered the crown prince to wear the nine-emblem robe and tasseled cap when attending court congratulations. Cheng and Qiu Zhongqi of the Rituals Section argued: "Wearing the tasseled cap at court is in fact prescribed in the canonical texts."

sentences.zh: 秦除六冕，漢明還備。

translations.literal: "Qin abolished the six caps with tassels; Han Ming restored them in full."
translations.idiomatic: "The Qin abolished the six tasseled caps; Emperor Ming of Han restored them in full."

sentences.zh: 魏晉以來，不欲令臣下服衮冕，故位公者加侍官。

translations.literal: "From Wei and Jin onward, they did not wish to let subjects below wear robe and cap with tassels, so those of duke rank were given attendant offices in addition."
translations.idiomatic: "From Wei and Jin onward, they did not wish subjects to wear the robe and tasseled cap, so men of duke rank were given additional attendant offices instead."

sentences.zh: 今皇太子禮絕羣后，宜遵聖王盛典，革近代之制。

translations.literal: "Now the crown prince's ritual stands above all the consorts; he ought to follow the great models of the sage kings and reform the institutions of recent times."
translations.idiomatic: "The crown prince's ritual now stands above all consorts; he ought to follow the great models of the sage kings and reform the institutions of recent times."

sentences.zh: 」尋轉著作正員郎，兼官如故。

translations.literal: " Soon he was transferred to Regular Gentleman of the Composition Office, with his concurrent posts as before.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon he was transferred to Regular Gentleman of the Composition Office, retaining his concurrent posts as before.

sentences.zh: 除安成太守，轉劉韞撫軍長史，加綏遠將軍、襄陽太守，竝不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Administrator of Ancheng, transferred to Chief Clerk on the Pacification Army staff of Liu Yun, and additionally made General Who Pacifies the Distance and Grand Administrator of Xiangyang—all of which he declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Administrator of Ancheng, then transferred to Chief Clerk on Liu Yun's Pacification Army staff, and additionally offered the posts of General Who Pacifies the Distance and Grand Administrator of Xiangyang—all of which he declined.

sentences.zh: 仍轉劉秉後軍長史、東海太守。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Chief Clerk of the Rear Army under Liu Bing and Grand Administrator of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Chief Clerk of the Rear Army under Liu Bing and Grand Administrator of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Assistant Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Assistant Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，驃騎諮議沈憲等坐家奴客爲劫，子弟被劾，憲等晏然。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, Advisory Counselor on the Rapid Cavalry staff Shen Xian and others were implicated because household slaves and retainers committed robbery; their sons and younger brothers were impeached, yet Xian and the others were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyuan, Advisory Counselor Shen Xian and others on the Rapid Cavalry staff were implicated because household slaves and retainers committed robbery; their sons and younger brothers were impeached, yet Xian and the others remained unconcerned.

sentences.zh: 左丞任遐奏澄不糾，請免澄官。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Ren Xia memorialized that Cheng had failed to investigate and asked that Cheng be removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Ren Xia memorialized that Cheng had failed to investigate and requested that Cheng be dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 澄上表自理曰：

translations.literal: Cheng submitted a memorial in his own defense, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Cheng submitted a memorial in his own defense, stating:

sentences.zh: :　　周稱舊章，漢言故事，爰自河雒，降逮淮海，朝之憲度，動尚先准。

translations.literal: Zhou was called the old statutes; Han spoke of precedents. From the He and Luo down to the Huai and sea, the court's laws and measures always looked to prior standards.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou spoke of old statutes; the Han spoke of precedents. From the He and Luo down to the Huai and sea, the court's laws and measures always looked to prior standards.

sentences.zh: 若乃任情違古，率意專造，豈謂酌諸故實，擇其茂典？

translations.literal: If one follows personal inclination against antiquity and acts on impulse in private invention, how can this be called weighing the old facts and selecting their flourishing models?
translations.idiomatic: If one follows personal inclination against antiquity and acts on impulse in private invention, how can this be called weighing the old facts and selecting their finest models?

sentences.zh: :　　案遐啓彈新除諮議參驃騎大將軍軍事沈憲、太子庶子沈曠幷弟息，敕付建康，而憲被使，曠受假，俱無歸罪事狀。

translations.literal: According to Xia's memorial impeaching the newly appointed Advisory Counselor and staff officer on the Grand General of Rapid Cavalry's military affairs Shen Xian, the Crown Prince's Household Companion Shen Kuang, and their younger brothers and sons: an edict handed the case to Jiankang, yet Xian was on assignment and Kuang was on leave—neither had circumstances warranting conviction.
translations.idiomatic: According to Xia's impeachment of the newly appointed Advisory Counselor and staff officer on the Grand General of Rapid Cavalry's military affairs Shen Xian, the Crown Prince's Household Companion Shen Kuang, and their younger brothers and sons: an edict referred the case to Jiankang, yet Xian was on assignment and Kuang was on leave—neither had circumstances warranting conviction.

sentences.zh: 臣以不糾憲等爲失。

translations.literal: Your subject considers failure to investigate Xian and the others a fault.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject acknowledges that failure to investigate Xian and the others was a fault.

sentences.zh: 伏尋晉、宋左丞案奏，不乏於時，其及中丞者，從來殆無。

translations.literal: I humbly examine the case memorials of Left Assistants under Jin and Song: they were not lacking in their time, but those reaching the Imperial Censor have almost never existed.
translations.idiomatic: On examining the case memorials of Left Assistants under Jin and Song, they were plentiful in their time, but those reaching the Imperial Censor have almost never existed.

sentences.zh: 王獻之習達朝章，近代之宗，其爲左丞，彈司徒屬王濛憚罰自解，屬疾遊行，初不及中丞。

translations.literal: Wang Xianzhi was versed in court regulations, a master of recent times. As Left Assistant he impeached Wang Meng, an aide of the Minister of Education, who feared punishment and resigned of his own accord for illness and travel—at first it did not reach the Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianzhi, versed in court regulations and a master of recent times, served as Left Assistant and impeached Wang Meng, an aide of the Minister of Education, who feared punishment and resigned on grounds of illness and travel—the case at first did not reach the Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 桓祕不奔山陵，左丞鄭襲不彈祕，直彈中丞孔欣時，又云別攝蘭臺檢校，此徑彈中丞之謂。

translations.literal: Huan Mi did not hurry to the imperial tombs; Left Assistant Zheng Xi did not impeach Mi but impeached Imperial Censor Kong Xin directly. It also said he separately took charge of Orchid Terrace inspection—this is what is meant by impeaching the Imperial Censor directly.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Mi did not hurry to the imperial tombs; Left Assistant Zheng Xi did not impeach Mi but impeached Imperial Censor Kong Xin directly, also stating that he separately took charge of Orchid Terrace inspection—this is what is meant by impeaching the Imperial Censor directly.

sentences.zh: 唯左丞庾登之奏鎮北檀道濟北伐不進，致虎牢陷沒，蕃岳宰臣，引咎謝諐，而責帥之劾，曾莫奏聞，請收治道濟，免中丞何萬歲。

translations.literal: Only Left Assistant Yu Dengzhi memorialized that Tan Daoji, Pacification General of the North, did not advance on the northern campaign and caused Tiger Fortress to fall; the frontier commanders and chief ministers accepted blame and apologized for their fault, yet the impeachment blaming the commander was never reported. He asked that Daoji be arrested and tried, and that Imperial Censor He Wansui be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Only Left Assistant Yu Dengzhi memorialized that Tan Daoji, Pacification General of the North, failed to advance on the northern campaign and caused Tiger Fortress to fall; the frontier commanders and chief ministers accepted blame, yet the impeachment blaming the commander was never reported. He requested that Daoji be arrested and tried and that Imperial Censor He Wansui be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 夫山陵情敬之極，北伐專征之大，祕霸季之貴，道濟元勳之盛，所以咎及南司，事非常憲，然祕事猶非及中丞也。

translations.literal: Imperial tombs are the utmost in emotional reverence; the northern campaign is the greatest of special expeditions. Mi was noble as a hegemon of the season; Daoji was grand as a founding merit-holder. Therefore blame reached the southern office—matters outside the usual statutes—yet even Mi's case still did not reach the Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial tombs represent the utmost in filial reverence; the northern campaign was the greatest of special expeditions. Mi was noble as a regional hegemon; Daoji was eminent as a founding merit-holder. Therefore blame reached the Censorate—matters outside ordinary statutes—yet even Mi's case still did not reach the Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 今若以此爲例，恐人之貴賤，事之輕重，物有其倫，不可相方。

translations.literal: If one now takes this as a precedent, I fear that men's noble and base status and affairs' light and heavy weight each have their proper categories and cannot be measured against one another.
translations.idiomatic: If one now takes this as a precedent, men's noble and base status and the light or heavy weight of affairs each have their proper categories and cannot be measured against one another.

sentences.zh: :　　左丞江奧彈段景文，又彈裴方明；

translations.literal: Left Assistant Jiang Ao impeached Duan Jingwen and also impeached Pei Fangming;
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Jiang Ao impeached Duan Jingwen and also impeached Pei Fangming;

sentences.zh: 左丞甄法崇彈蕭珍，又彈杜驥，又彈段國，又彈范文伯；

translations.literal: Left Assistant Zhen Fachong impeached Xiao Zhen, also impeached Du Ji, also impeached Duan Guo, and also impeached Fan Wenbo;
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Zhen Fachong impeached Xiao Zhen, Du Ji, Duan Guo, and Fan Wenbo;

sentences.zh: 左丞羊玄保又彈蕭汪；

translations.literal: Left Assistant Yang Xuanbao also impeached Xiao Wang;
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Yang Xuanbao also impeached Xiao Wang;

sentences.zh: 左丞殷景熙彈張仲仁；

translations.literal: Left Assistant Yin Jingxi impeached Zhang Zhongren;
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Yin Jingxi impeached Zhang Zhongren;

sentences.zh: 兼左丞何承天彈呂萬齡。

translations.literal: Concurrent Left Assistant He Chengtian impeached Lü Wanling.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent Left Assistant He Chengtian impeached Lü Wanling.

sentences.zh: 竝不歸罪，皆爲重劾。

translations.literal: None resulted in conviction; all were serious impeachments.
translations.idiomatic: None resulted in conviction; all were serious impeachments.

sentences.zh: 凡茲十彈，差是憲、曠之比，悉無及中丞之議。

translations.literal: Of these ten impeachments in all, they are roughly comparable to Xian and Kuang; none included discussion reaching the Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Of these ten impeachments altogether, they are roughly comparable to the cases of Xian and Kuang; none included proceedings reaching the Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 左丞荀萬秋、劉藏、江謐彈王僧朗、王雲之、陶寶度，不及中丞，最是近例之明者。

translations.literal: Left Assistants Xun Wanqiu, Liu Zang, and Jiang Mi impeached Wang Senglang, Wang Yunzhi, and Tao Baodu without reaching the Imperial Censor—the clearest of recent precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistants Xun Wanqiu, Liu Zang, and Jiang Mi impeached Wang Senglang, Wang Yunzhi, and Tao Baodu without reaching the Imperial Censor—the clearest of recent precedents.

sentences.zh: 謐彈在今龕之後，事行聖照。

translations.literal: Mi's impeachment came after the present niche; the matter proceeded under sagely illumination.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's impeachment came after the present reign; the matter proceeded under imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 遠取十奏，近徵二案，自宜依以爲體，豈得捨而不遵？

translations.literal: Taking ten memorials from afar and citing two cases from near at hand, one ought by rights to take these as the standard—how could one discard them and not follow them?
translations.idiomatic: Taking ten memorials from the distant past and citing two cases from recent times, one ought to take these as the standard—how could one discard them and not follow them?

sentences.zh: :　　臣竊此人乏，謬奉國憲。

translations.literal: Your subject, though personally deficient, has wrongly received charge of the state's laws.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, though personally deficient, has wrongly been entrusted with the state's laws.

sentences.zh: 今遐所糾，旣行一時，若默而不言，則向爲來准，後人被繩，方當追請，素餐之責，貽塵千載。

translations.literal: What Xia now impeaches has already been put into effect for the moment. If I remain silent and do not speak, then what was done before becomes the standard for what follows; later men will be bound by the cord, and only then will they pursue inquiry. The blame of eating salary without work would stain the dust for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: What Xia now impeaches has already been put into effect. If I remain silent, what was done before becomes the standard for the future; later men will be bound by it, and only then will they pursue inquiry. The blame of holding office without merit would stain one's name for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 所以備舉顯例，弘通國典，雖有愚心，不在微躬。

translations.literal: Therefore I fully cite outstanding examples and broadly expound the state's statutes. Though I have a foolish heart, it is not for my slight person alone.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I fully cite outstanding examples and broadly expound the state's statutes. Though my intent may be foolish, it is not for my personal sake alone.

sentences.zh: 請出臣表付外詳議。

translations.literal: I ask that my memorial be sent out for detailed deliberation by the outer offices.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that my memorial be sent out for detailed deliberation by the outer offices.

sentences.zh: 若所陳非謬，裁由天鑒。

translations.literal: If what I have stated is not in error, let the decision rest with Heaven's discernment.
translations.idiomatic: If what I have stated is not in error, let the decision rest with Heaven's discernment.

sentences.zh: 詔委外詳議。

translations.literal: An edict entrusted the matter to detailed deliberation by the outer offices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict entrusted the matter to detailed deliberation by the outer offices.

sentences.zh: 尚書令褚淵奏：「宋世左丞荀伯子彈彭城令張道欣等，坐界劫累發不禽，免道欣等官；

translations.literal: Minister of the Masters of Writing Chu Yuan memorialized: "In Song times Left Assistant Xun Bozi impeached Zhang Daoxin, Magistrate of Pengcheng, and others, who were implicated because border robberies repeatedly broke out and were not captured; Daoxin and the others were removed from office;"
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Masters of Writing Chu Yuan memorialized: "In Song times Left Assistant Xun Bozi impeached Zhang Daoxin, Magistrate of Pengcheng, and others for repeated border robberies that were not captured; Daoxin and the others were dismissed;"

sentences.zh: 中丞王准不糾，亦免官。

translations.literal: "Imperial Censor Wang Zhun failed to investigate and was also removed from office."
translations.idiomatic: "Imperial Censor Wang Zhun failed to investigate and was also dismissed."

sentences.zh: 左丞羊玄保彈豫州刺史管義之譙梁羣盜，免義之官；

translations.literal: "Left Assistant Yang Xuanbao impeached Guan Yizhi, Inspector of Yuzhou, for bandits in Qiao and Liang; Yizhi was removed from office;"
translations.idiomatic: "Left Assistant Yang Xuanbao impeached Guan Yizhi, Inspector of Yuzhou, for bandits in Qiao and Liang; Yizhi was dismissed;"

sentences.zh: 中丞傅隆不糾，亦免隆官。

translations.literal: "Imperial Censor Fu Long failed to investigate and Long was also removed from office."
translations.idiomatic: "Imperial Censor Fu Long failed to investigate and was also dismissed."

sentences.zh: 左丞羊玄保又彈兖州刺史鄭從之濫上布及加課租綿，免從之官；

translations.literal: "Left Assistant Yang Xuanbao again impeached Zheng Congzhi, Inspector of Yanzhou, for improperly submitting cloth and imposing extra tax levies of silk; Congzhi was removed from office;"
translations.idiomatic: "Left Assistant Yang Xuanbao again impeached Zheng Congzhi, Inspector of Yanzhou, for improperly submitting cloth and imposing extra silk taxes; Congzhi was dismissed;"

sentences.zh: 中丞傅隆不糾，免隆官。

translations.literal: "Imperial Censor Fu Long failed to investigate and Long was removed from office."
translations.idiomatic: "Imperial Censor Fu Long failed to investigate and was dismissed."

sentences.zh: 左丞陸展彈建康令丘珍孫、丹陽尹孔山士劫發不禽，免珍孫、山士官；

translations.literal: "Left Assistant Lu Zhan impeached Qiu Zhensun, Magistrate of Jiankang, and Kong Shanshi, Administrator of Danyang, because robberies broke out and were not captured; Zhensun and Shanshi were removed from office;"
translations.idiomatic: "Left Assistant Lu Zhan impeached Qiu Zhensun, Magistrate of Jiankang, and Kong Shanshi, Administrator of Danyang, because robberies broke out and were not captured; Zhensun and Shanshi were dismissed;"

sentences.zh: 中丞何勗不糾，亦免勗官。

translations.literal: "Imperial Censor He Xu failed to investigate and Xu was also removed from office."
translations.idiomatic: "Imperial Censor He Xu failed to investigate and was also dismissed."

sentences.zh: 左丞劉矇彈青州刺史劉道隆失火燒府庫，免道隆官；

translations.literal: "Left Assistant Liu Meng impeached Liu Daolong, Inspector of Qingzhou, because fire burned the government storehouses; Daolong was removed from office;"
translations.idiomatic: "Left Assistant Liu Meng impeached Liu Daolong, Inspector of Qingzhou, because fire burned the government storehouses; Daolong was dismissed;"

sentences.zh: 中丞蕭惠開不糾，免惠開官。

translations.literal: "Imperial Censor Xiao Huikai failed to investigate and Huikai was removed from office."
translations.idiomatic: "Imperial Censor Xiao Huikai failed to investigate and was dismissed."

sentences.zh: 左丞徐爰彈右衞將軍薛安都屬疾不直，免安都官；

translations.literal: "Left Assistant Xu Ai impeached Xue Andu, General of the Right Guards, for claiming illness and not attending duty; Andu was removed from office;"
translations.idiomatic: "Left Assistant Xu Ai impeached Xue Andu, General of the Right Guards, for claiming illness and not attending duty; Andu was dismissed;"

sentences.zh: 中丞張永結免。

translations.literal: "Imperial Censor Zhang Yong was bound and removed."
translations.idiomatic: "Imperial Censor Zhang Yong was bound and dismissed."

sentences.zh: 澄謏聞膚見，貽撓後昆，上掩皇明，下籠朝識，請以見事免澄所居官。

translations.literal: "Cheng's shallow hearing and skin-deep views obstruct later generations, cover up above the emperor's brilliance, and cage below the court's understanding. I ask that on the basis of the present matter Cheng be removed from the office he holds."
translations.idiomatic: "Cheng's shallow hearing and superficial views obstruct later generations, obscure the emperor's brilliance above, and mislead the court below. I ask that on the basis of the present matter Cheng be dismissed from the office he holds."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「澄表據多謬，不足深劾，可白衣領職。」

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Cheng's memorial citations are largely in error and do not warrant deep impeachment; he may serve in plain clothes while retaining his duties.""
translations.idiomatic: " An edict stated: "Cheng's memorial citations are largely in error and do not warrant severe punishment; he may serve in plain clothes while retaining his duties."

sentences.zh: 明年，轉給事中，祕書監，遷吏部。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Director of the Palace Library, and promoted to the Ministry of Officials.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Director of the Palace Library, and promoted to the Ministry of Officials.

sentences.zh: 四年，復爲祕書監，領國子博士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again became Director of the Palace Library and concurrently Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he again became Director of the Palace Library and concurrently Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 遷都官尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 出爲輔國將軍、鎮北鎮軍二府長史，廷尉，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk of the two offices of the General Who Assists the State and the Pacification Generals of the North and the Army, Minister of Punishments, and concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as Chief Clerk of the offices of the General Who Assists the State and the Pacification Generals of the North and the Army, as Minister of Punishments, and concurrently as General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，轉度支尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongming he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋領國子博士。

translations.literal: Soon he concurrently held Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also served concurrently as Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時國學置鄭王《易》，杜服《春秋》，何氏《公羊》，麋氏《穀梁》，鄭玄《孝經》。

translations.literal: At that time the Imperial University established Zheng and Wang commentaries on the Changes, Du and Fu on the Spring and Autumn, the He clan on the Gongyang, the Mi clan on the Guliang, and Zheng Xuan on the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Imperial University taught Zheng and Wang commentaries on the Changes, Du and Fu on the Spring and Autumn, the He clan on the Gongyang, the Mi clan on the Guliang, and Zheng Xuan on the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 澄謂尚書令王儉曰：「《孝經》，小學之類，不宜列在帝典。

translations.literal: Cheng said to Wang Jian, Minister of the Masters of Writing: "The Classic of Filial Piety belongs to the category of elementary learning and ought not to be listed among the emperor's canons."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said to Wang Jian, Minister of the Masters of Writing: "The Classic of Filial Piety belongs to elementary learning and ought not to be listed among the emperor's canons."

sentences.zh: 」乃與儉書論之曰：

translations.literal: " Thereupon he wrote to Jian discussing it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he wrote to Jian discussing the matter, stating:

sentences.zh: :　　《易》近取諸身，遠取諸物，彌天地之道，通萬物之情。

translations.literal: The Changes takes from the near in the person and from the far in things; it fills the Way of Heaven and Earth and penetrates the feelings of the ten thousand things.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes draws from what is near in the person and from what is far in things; it encompasses the Way of Heaven and Earth and penetrates the feelings of the ten thousand things.

sentences.zh: 自商瞿至田何，其閒五傳。

translations.literal: From Shang Qu to Tian He, between them were five transmissions.
translations.idiomatic: From Shang Qu to Tian He, there were five transmissions in between.

sentences.zh: 年未爲遠，無訛雜之失；

translations.literal: The years are not yet remote, and there are no errors of mixture;
translations.idiomatic: The years are not yet remote, and there are no errors of mixture;

sentences.zh: 秦所不焚，無崩壞之弊。

translations.literal: what Qin did not burn has no flaw of collapse and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: what Qin did not burn suffers no flaw of collapse and ruin.

sentences.zh: 雖有異家之學，同以象數爲宗。

translations.literal: Although there are different schools of learning, all alike take images and numbers as their foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Although there are different schools, all alike take images and numbers as their foundation.

sentences.zh: 數百年後，乃有王弼。

translations.literal: Several hundred years later there was Wang Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred years later came Wang Bi.

sentences.zh: 王濟云弼所悟者多，何必能頓廢前儒。

translations.literal: Wang Ji said that what Bi understood was much, but why must one suddenly abolish the earlier Confucians?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji said that Bi understood a great deal, but why must one suddenly abolish the earlier Confucians?

sentences.zh: 若謂易道盡於王弼，方須大論，意者無乃仁智殊見。

translations.literal: If one says the Way of the Changes is exhausted in Wang Bi, then a great discussion is needed; perhaps benevolence and wisdom see differently.
translations.idiomatic: If one says the Way of the Changes is fully contained in Wang Bi, a great debate is needed; perhaps benevolence and wisdom simply see differently.

sentences.zh: 易道無體不可以一體求，屢遷不可以一遷執也。

translations.literal: The Way of the Changes has no fixed form and cannot be sought in a single form; it shifts repeatedly and cannot be grasped in a single shift.
translations.idiomatic: The Way of the Changes has no fixed form and cannot be sought in a single form; it shifts repeatedly and cannot be grasped at a single point.

sentences.zh: 晉太興四年，太常荀崧請置《周易》鄭玄注博士，行乎前代，于時政由王、庾，皆俊神清識，能言玄遠，捨輔嗣而用康成，豈其妄然。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taixing of Jin, Minister of Ceremonies Xun Song requested establishment of an Erudite for Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Book of Changes. This was practiced in former generations; at that time government was in the hands of the Wang and Yu clans—all were brilliant spirits with clear understanding, able to speak of the abstruse and far-reaching. They set aside Fusi and used Kangcheng—how could this have been reckless?
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taixing of Jin, Minister of Ceremonies Xun Song requested an Erudite for Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Book of Changes. This had been practiced in former generations; at that time government was in the hands of the Wang and Yu clans—all brilliant men of clear understanding, able to discourse on the abstruse. They set aside Wang Bi and used Zheng Xuan—how could this have been reckless?

sentences.zh: 太元立王肅易，當以在玄、弼之閒。

translations.literal: In Taiyuan Wang Su's Changes was established; it should be placed between Xuan and Bi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiyuan era Wang Su's Changes was established; it should be placed between Zheng Xuan and Wang Bi.

sentences.zh: 元嘉建學之始，玄、弼兩立。

translations.literal: At the beginning of establishing the school in Yuanjia, Xuan and Bi were both established.
translations.idiomatic: When the school was established at the beginning of Yuanjia, Zheng Xuan and Wang Bi were both taught.

sentences.zh: 逮顏延之爲祭酒，黜鄭置王，意在貴玄，事成敗儒。

translations.literal: When Yan Yanzhi became Libationer, he dismissed Zheng and established Wang; the intent was to honor the abstruse, and the result was defeat for the Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Yanzhi became Libationer, he dismissed Zheng and established Wang; the intent was to honor the abstruse school, and the result was a setback for Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 今若不大弘儒風，則無所立學，衆經皆儒，惟《易》獨玄，玄不可棄，儒不可缺。

translations.literal: If one does not now greatly expand the Confucian wind, there is nowhere to establish learning. All the classics are Confucian; only the Changes alone is abstruse. The abstruse cannot be abandoned; the Confucian cannot be lacking.
translations.idiomatic: If one does not now greatly promote Confucian learning, there is nowhere to establish the school. All the classics are Confucian; only the Changes is abstruse. The abstruse cannot be abandoned; Confucian learning cannot be omitted.

sentences.zh: 謂宜竝存，所以合無體之義。

translations.literal: I say both ought to be preserved together—thus conforming to the meaning of having no fixed form.
translations.idiomatic: I say both ought to be preserved together—thus conforming to the meaning of having no fixed form.

sentences.zh: 且弼於注經中已舉《繫辭》，故不復別注。

translations.literal: Moreover, Bi in commenting on the classic already cited the Appended Phrases, and therefore did not comment on them separately.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Wang Bi in his commentary on the classic already cited the Appended Phrases and therefore did not comment on them separately.

sentences.zh: 今若專取弼《易》，則《繫》說無注。

translations.literal: If one now exclusively takes Bi's Changes, then the Appended Phrases commentary has no annotation.
translations.idiomatic: If one now exclusively adopts Wang Bi's Changes, then the Appended Phrases will have no commentary.

sentences.zh: :　　《左氏》太元取服虔，而兼取賈逵《經》，由服傳無《經》，雖在注中，而《傳》又有無《經》者故也。

translations.literal: For the Zuo Tradition, in Taiyuan they took Fu Qian and also took Jia Kui's Classic, because Fu's tradition lacked the Classic—although it was in the commentary, the Tradition also had places without the Classic.
translations.idiomatic: For the Zuo Tradition, in the Taiyuan era they adopted Fu Qian and also Jia Kui's Classic, because Fu's tradition lacked the Classic—although it appeared in the commentary, the Tradition also had passages without the Classic.

sentences.zh: 今留服而去賈，則《經》有所闕。

translations.literal: If one now keeps Fu and removes Jia, then the Classic will have gaps.
translations.idiomatic: If one now keeps Fu and removes Jia, the Classic will have gaps.

sentences.zh: 案杜預注《傳》，王弼注《易》，俱是晚出，竝貴後生。

translations.literal: Du Yu's commentary on the Tradition and Wang Bi's commentary on the Changes both appeared late and alike honor later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu's commentary on the Tradition and Wang Bi's commentary on the Changes both appeared late and alike favor later generations.

sentences.zh: 杜之異古，未如王之奪實，祖述前儒，特舉其違。

translations.literal: Du's divergence from antiquity was not like Wang's seizure of substance; he traced and expounded the earlier Confucians and specially cited their departures.
translations.idiomatic: Du's divergence from antiquity was not like Wang's rejection of substance; he followed the earlier Confucians and specially cited their departures.

sentences.zh: 又《釋例》之作，所弘惟深。

translations.literal: Moreover, his composition Explanatory Examples expounds only what is deep.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, his Explanatory Examples expounds only what is profound.

sentences.zh: :　　《穀梁》太元舊有麋信注，顏益以范寧，麋猶如故。

translations.literal: For the Guliang, in Taiyuan there was formerly Mi Xin's commentary; Yan added Fan Ning to it, while Mi remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: For the Guliang, in the Taiyuan era there was Mi Xin's commentary; Yan Yanzhi added Fan Ning's commentary, while Mi's remained as before.

sentences.zh: 顏論閏分范注，當以同我者親。

translations.literal: Yan discussed intercalary months and divided Fan's commentary; one ought to be close to those who agree with oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Yan discussed intercalary months and divided Fan's commentary; one ought to favor those who agree with oneself.

sentences.zh: 常謂《穀梁》劣《公羊》，爲注者又不盡善。

translations.literal: He constantly said the Guliang was inferior to the Gongyang, and those who commented on it were not entirely good.
translations.idiomatic: He often said the Guliang was inferior to the Gongyang, and its commentators were not entirely adequate.

sentences.zh: 竟無及《公羊》之有何休，恐不足兩立。

translations.literal: In the end none matched the Gongyang's having He Xiu; I fear it is not enough to establish both.
translations.idiomatic: In the end none matched the Gongyang's having He Xiu; I fear the two cannot stand together.

sentences.zh: 必謂范善，便當除麋。

translations.literal: If one must say Fan is good, then Mi should be removed.
translations.idiomatic: If one insists Fan is superior, then Mi should be removed.

sentences.zh: :　　世有一《孝經》，題爲鄭玄注，觀其用辭，不與注書相類。

translations.literal: In the world there is a Classic of Filial Piety titled as Zheng Xuan's commentary; observing its wording, it does not resemble his commentarial books.
translations.idiomatic: There is a Classic of Filial Piety in circulation titled as Zheng Xuan's commentary; its wording does not resemble his other commentarial works.

sentences.zh: 案玄自序所注衆書，亦無《孝經》。

translations.literal: According to Xuan's own preface listing the many books he commented on, there is also no Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: According to Xuan's own preface listing the books he commented on, the Classic of Filial Piety is not included.

sentences.zh: 儉答曰：「《易》體微遠，實貫羣籍，施、孟異聞，周、韓殊旨，豈可專據小王，便爲該備？

translations.literal: Jian replied: "The Changes' form is subtle and far-reaching and in fact runs through all books. Shi and Meng had different transmissions; Zhou and Han had different aims—how could one exclusively rely on young Wang and consider it complete?"
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied: "The Changes is subtle and far-reaching and in fact runs through all the classics. Shi and Meng had different transmissions; Zhou and Han had different aims—how could one rely exclusively on Wang Bi and consider the field complete?"

sentences.zh: 依舊存鄭，高同來說。

translations.literal: "Preserve Zheng as before—this is the lofty doctrine that has come down."
translations.idiomatic: "Preserve Zheng as before—this is the established doctrine handed down."

sentences.zh: 元凱注傳，超邁前儒，若不列學官，其可廢矣。

translations.literal: "Yuankai's commentary on the Tradition surpasses the earlier Confucians; if it is not listed among the school officials, how could it be abandoned?"
translations.idiomatic: "Du Yu's commentary on the Tradition surpasses the earlier Confucians; if it is not listed among the school officials, how could it be abandoned?"

sentences.zh: 賈氏注《經》，世所罕習，《穀梁》小書，無俟兩注，存麋略范，率由舊式。

translations.literal: "The Jia clan's commentary on the Classic is rarely practiced in the world. The Guliang is a small book and has no need of two commentaries; keep Mi and set Fan aside—follow the old pattern."
translations.idiomatic: "Jia Kui's commentary on the Classic is rarely studied today. The Guliang is a minor text and needs no dual commentary; keep Mi and set Fan aside—follow the established pattern."

sentences.zh: 凡此諸義，竝同雅論。

translations.literal: "All these points alike accord with refined discussion."
translations.idiomatic: "All these points accord with established scholarly opinion."

sentences.zh: 疑《孝經》非鄭所注，僕以此書明百行之首，實人倫所先，《七略》、《藝文》竝陳之六藝，不與《蒼頡》、《凡將》之流也。

translations.literal: "I suspect the Classic of Filial Piety is not Zheng's commentary. I consider this book to clarify the head of the hundred conduct and is truly what human relations put first. The Seven Summaries and Bibliographic Treatise both list it among the Six Arts—it is not of the sort of Cangjie or Fansjiang."
translations.idiomatic: "I suspect the Classic of Filial Piety is not by Zheng Xuan. I consider this book to clarify the foremost of the hundred virtues and to stand at the head of human relations. The Seven Summaries and Bibliographic Treatise both list it among the Six Arts—it is not in the class of Cangjie or Fansjiang."

sentences.zh: 鄭注虛實，前代不嫌，意謂可安，仍舊立置。」

translations.literal: "Whether Zheng's commentary is authentic or spurious, former generations did not mind; I consider it acceptable and that it should remain established as before."
translations.idiomatic: "Whether Zheng's commentary is authentic or spurious, former generations did not mind; I consider it acceptable and that it should remain in place as before."

sentences.zh: 儉自以博聞多識，讀書過澄。

translations.literal: Jian considered himself broad in hearing and rich in knowledge, and that his reading surpassed Cheng's.
translations.idiomatic: Jian considered himself widely learned and believed he had read more than Cheng.

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「僕年少來無事，唯以讀書爲業。

translations.literal: Cheng said: "From youth I have had no other business and take reading alone as my occupation."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said: "From my youth I have had no other occupation but reading."

sentences.zh: 且年已倍令君，令君少便鞅掌王務，雖復一覽便諳，然見卷軸未必多僕。

translations.literal: "Moreover, my years are already double those of Your Lordship. Your Lordship from youth has been busy with royal affairs; though you may grasp a text in one reading, yet the scrolls you have seen may not necessarily exceed mine."
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover, I am already twice your age. You have been busy with state affairs since youth; though you may master a text at a single reading, the scrolls you have seen may not exceed mine."

sentences.zh: 」儉集學士何憲等盛自商略，澄待儉語畢，然後談所遺漏數百千條，皆儉所未睹，儉乃歎服。

translations.literal: " Jian gathered the scholars He Xian and others and engaged in vigorous discussion. Cheng waited until Jian had finished speaking, then discussed several hundred or thousand items that had been omitted—all of which Jian had never seen—and Jian then sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian gathered the scholars He Xian and others for vigorous discussion. Cheng waited until Jian had finished, then cited several hundred or thousand omitted items that Jian had never seen, and Jian sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 儉在尚書省，出巾箱机案雜服飾，令學士隷事，事多者與之，人人各得一兩物，澄後來，更出諸人所不知事復各數條，幷奪物將去。

translations.literal: When Jian was in the Masters of Writing office, he brought out kerchief-boxes, desk items, and miscellaneous garments and ornaments and had the scholars record them; those with many items received them, and each person got one or two objects. Cheng came later and produced several more items in each category that none of the others knew, and also took objects away with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian was in the Masters of Writing office, he brought out kerchief-boxes, desk items, and miscellaneous garments and ornaments and had the scholars record them; those who identified the most received rewards, and each person got one or two objects. Cheng arrived later, identified several more items in each category that none of the others knew, and also took objects away with him.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎常侍，祕書監，吳郡中正，光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant at the Palace Library, Director of the Palace Library, Rectifier of Wu Commandery, and Grand Master for the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Regular Attendant at the Palace Library, Director of the Palace Library, Rectifier of Wu Commandery, and Grand Master for the Palace.

sentences.zh: 加給事中，中正如故。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, with his rectifier post as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, retaining his post as rectifier.

sentences.zh: 尋領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Soon he concurrently held Libationer of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also served as Libationer of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 以竟陵王子良得古器，小口方腹而底平，可將七八升，以問澄，澄曰：「北名服匿，單于以與蘇武。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, obtained an ancient vessel—small mouth, square belly, and flat base, holding about seven or eight sheng—he asked Cheng about it. Cheng said: "In the north it is called funu; the chanyu gave it to Su Wu."
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, obtained an ancient vessel with a small mouth, square belly, and flat base that held about seven or eight sheng, he asked Cheng about it. Cheng said: "In the north it is called funu; the chanyu gave it to Su Wu."

sentences.zh: 」子良後詳視器底，有字髣彿可識，如澄所言。

translations.literal: " Later Ziliang examined the vessel's base in detail; there were characters dimly recognizable, just as Cheng had said.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Ziliang examined the base of the vessel in detail and found characters dimly recognizable, just as Cheng had said.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，以老疾，轉光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，未拜，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang, on account of age and illness he was transferred to Grand Master for the Palace and additionally made Regular Attendant at the Palace Library, but before accepting office he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang, on account of age and illness he was transferred to Grand Master for the Palace and additionally offered Regular Attendant at the Palace Library, but before accepting office he died.

sentences.zh: 年七十。

translations.literal: He was seventy years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy.

sentences.zh: 諡靖子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Jingzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Jingzi.

sentences.zh: 澄當世稱爲碩學，讀《易》三年不解文義，欲撰《宋書》竟不成，王儉戲之曰：「陸公，書廚也。

translations.literal: Cheng was called a great scholar in his age, yet after reading the Changes for three years he did not understand its literary meaning; he wished to compile a Book of Song but in the end did not complete it. Wang Jian joked of him: "Master Lu is a book cupboard."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was acclaimed in his age as a great scholar, yet after three years of reading the Changes he still did not understand its meaning; he wished to compile a Book of Song but never finished it. Wang Jian joked: "Master Lu is a walking library."

sentences.zh: 」家多墳籍，人所罕見。

translations.literal: " His household had many ancient books rarely seen by others.
translations.idiomatic: " His household possessed many rare books seldom seen by others.

sentences.zh: 撰地理書及雜傳，死後乃出。
